profile_md: **Cambridge has no institution-wide employer-project scheme; provision is concentrated in a few programme-embedded routes.** Cambridge Judge Business School runs the densest set: the MBA Global Consulting Project (4-5 students, ~4 weeks, hosts such as WHO and Uber) and Cambridge Venture Project (5-6 students, ~6 weeks, local businesses), the MFin Group Consulting Project, the MPhil in Management Consulting Project, the undergraduate Management Studies Tripos project (teams of 3-4 for external organisations), and the MPhil in Technology Policy Final Group Project (clients including Cabinet Office, Ofcom, Arm). Each is part of a degree, uses a central client-proposal process with 2026/27 calls, and relies on external organisations as clients who receive the output. Outside business, the Computer Science Tripos Part IB group project is the standout: a compulsory seven-week team project for an assigned industry client, with 2026 clients including Nokia Bell Labs and Bending Spoons. Further routes exist in Engineering (IfM MET/ISMM company projects, ESD MPhil Client Project), Bioscience Enterprise and Public Policy/Conservation Leadership, but these lack dated current evidence. The university-wide i-Teams programme (selective, extracurricular) has teams but internal research clients, so it does not meet the employer criterion. Access is by programme: none is open university-wide. Uncertain: credit weightings, EMBA duration, and current status of the engineering and social-science MPhil routes.
gaps: Further departmental instances likely (other MPhils, Engineering Part IIA group projects, Chemical Engineering, Medicine, Architecture, Law, Education not individually searched). Credit/weighting and 'compulsory' wording not retrieved for most JBS projects (inferred from core-curriculum placement). MET/ISMM, ESD, MBE, Bennett PAE and Conservation Leadership need dated 2025/26-2026/27 corroboration. Student societies (180 Degrees Consulting, Cambridge Consulting Network) and Cambridge Hub not verified. WebFetch unavailable; all evidence is search-index extract/paraphrase.
